rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here البيان is articulate, eloquent speech that expresses what is within; it is the ordinary means by which people learn the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: لأن البيان هو الذي بهيتمكن عادة من تعلم القرآن المراد به المنطق الفصيح المعرب عما في الضمير

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad reads creation of the human as identifying the learner and teaching البيان as explaining how the teaching occurs.
rows.anchor: وفي الإرشاد أن قوله تعالى : ( خلق الإنسان ) تعيين للمتعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching البيان means enabling people to express themselves and understand others, since that capacity underlies instruction in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتعليم البيان تمكين الإنسان من بيان نفسه ومن فهم بيان غيرهإذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that an object is omitted, the ones taught first may be the angels, who learned the Qur’an before the human was created.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بناءا على تنقدير المفعول المحذوف الملائكة المقربين إن تقديم تعليم القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence elegantly pairs heavenly matters with earthly ones; this arrangement also works if the omitted object is Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وفي النظم الجليل عليه حسن زائد حيث أنه تعالى ذكر أموراعلوية وأموراسفلية

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains البيان as good and evil.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : ( البيان ) الخير والشر

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains البيان as the path of guidance and the path of error.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج : سبيل الهدى وسبيل الضلالة

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yaman explains البيان as writing; the author dismisses these alternative glosses.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان : الكتابة والكل كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible gloss is the Qur’an itself, called a clarification elsewhere and repeated here to unpack the earlier statement about teaching the Qur’an; the author calls this very remote.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد به القرآنوقد سماه الله تعالى بيانا في قوله سبحانه : ( هذا بيان )

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah takes the human to be Adam and البيان to be knowledge of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : ( الإنسان ) آدم و ( البيان ) علم الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported explanations are that البيان comprises the names of all things or the ability to speak many languages.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( البيان ) أسماء الأشياء كلها وقيل : التكلم بلغات كثيرة

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: A view attributed to Ja‘far al-Sadiq identifies البيان as the Greatest Name by which everything was taught.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الاسم الأعظم الذي علم به كل شيء ونسبهذا إلى جعفر الصادق

rows.speaker: ابن كسيان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan identifies the human as Muhammad and takes البيان as explaining revelation, clarifying the Qur’an’s general or ambiguous passages, or the Qur’an itself.
rows.anchor: وقالابن كسيان : ( الإنسان ) محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the immediately apparent reading: the human generally is taught expressive speech, rather than the reported specialized meanings.
rows.anchor: المتبادر من الآيات الكريمة لا يخفى عليك ولا أظنك في مرية من تبادر ما ذكرناه فيها أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses about creating the human and teaching البيان each predicate something of the implicit subject الرحمن, as does teaching the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ثم إن كلا من الجملتين الأخيرتين خبر عن المبتدأكجملة ( علم القرآن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence about the plants prostrating is a predicate coordinated with the preceding predicate.
rows.anchor: فإن المعطوف على الخبر خبر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، أبو رزين
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Abu Razin take النجم as low-growing plants that emerge from the earth without a stem, and الشجر as plants with stems.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالنجم النبات الذي ينجم أي يظهر ويطلع من الأرض ولا ساق له وبالشجر النبات الذي له ساق وهو المروي عن ابن عباس وابن جبير وأبي رزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prostration is their submission to God’s will as it governs their natural behavior.
rows.anchor: والمراد بسجودهما انقيادهما له تعالى فيما يريد بهما طبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an explicit derivative metaphor: natural behavior is likened to a prostrator’s submission and reverence for its creator.
rows.anchor: شبه جريهما على مقتضى طبيعتهما بانقياد الساجد لخالقه وتعظيمه لهثم استعمل

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، الحسن
rows.claim: Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Hasan take النجم to mean the stars of the sky, whose prostration is their setting or the like.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة والحسن النجم نجم السماء وسجوده الغروب ونحوه

rows.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan explain the trees’ prostration through their shadows and their turning.
rows.anchor: وسجود الشجر بالظل واستداره عند مجاهد والحسن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In another report, Mujahid explains both prostrations as submission to whatever God naturally wills for them.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن مجاهدأن سجودهما عبارة عن انقيادهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority’s botanical interpretation is preferable because النجم is paired with الشجر, though the preceding mention of sun and moon suggests the familiar celestial meaning and creates an evident double meaning.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على تفسير النجم بما سمعت أولاقبل لأن اقترانه بالشجر يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier clauses omit conjunctions to enumerate separate blessings and stir gratitude; adding conjunctions might make them seem like one blessing, despite their close relation.
rows.anchor: وإخلاء الجمل الثانية والثالثة والرابعة عن العطف لورودها على نهج التعديد مع الإشارة إلى أن كلامما تضمنتهمستقلة تقتضي الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction between the fourth and fifth clauses pairs heavenly sun and moon with earthly plants and trees, both obedient to God’s command.
rows.anchor: وتوسيط العاطف بين الرابعة والخامسة رعاية لتناسبهما من حيث التقابل لما أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no verbal connective between the clauses because their semantic relation is unmistakable: the celestial bodies follow God’s reckoning and the plants prostrate to Him.
rows.anchor: وخلوهما عن الرابط اللفظي مع كونهما خبرين للتعويل على كمال قوة الارتباط المعنوي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the missing conjunctions as a way to enumerate and emphasize blessings one by one, prompting reflection and rebuking deniers; the ordered list resumes after that rhetorical stirring.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف : تبيينالما ذكره صاحب الكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause الشمس والقمر بحسبان is not a predicate of the implicit subject; al-Zamakhshari was explaining its semantic connection to the enumeration.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( الشمس والقمر بحسبان ) ليست من أخبار المبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the interpretation has gone too far, although the apparent wording of al-Zamakhshari’s discussion suggests that الشمس والقمر بحسبان is one of the predicates; he leaves the issue for reflection.
rows.anchor: وقد أبعدالمغزي فيما أرى إلآ أن ظاهر كلام الكشاف يقتضي كون قوله تعالى : ( الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means so that you do not transgress the balance’s due by going beyond proper bounds; أن is subjunctive, لا is negative, and an omitted purpose lām links it to God’s setting the balance.
rows.anchor: على أن ( أن ) ناصبة و ( لا ) نافية ولام العلة مقدرة متعلقة بقوله تعالى : ( وضع الميزان )

rows.speaker: ابن عطية، الزمخشري
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari allow أن to be explanatory and لا to be prohibitive.
rows.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية والزمخشري كون ( أن ) تفسيرية و ( لا ) ناهية

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that explanatory أن requires a preceding clause with a speech meaning, which is absent here.
rows.anchor: واعترضه أبو حيانبأنه لم يتقدم جملة فيها معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A response argues that setting the balance carries a speech meaning because it was done through revelation and the messengers’ instruction.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن وضع الميزان فيه ذلك لأنه بالوحي وإعلام الرسل عليهمالسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some insist the explanatory reading is necessary because setting a balance to prevent transgression seems incoherent, but the author rejects that objection.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن التفسير متعين لأنه لا معنى لوضع الميزان لئلا تطغوا في الميزان

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim reads ووضع الميزان with the ضاد vowelless and الميزان in the genitive, treating وضع as a verbal noun annexed to its object.
rows.anchor: قرأ إبراهيم ( ووضع الميزان ) بإسكان الضاد وخفض الميزان على أن ( وضع ) مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Ibrahim’s reading, if وضع is nominative it is apparently a subject with أن لا تطغوا as its predicate after an omitted preposition; if accusative, its governor is omitted or supplied.
rows.anchor: فإن كان مرفوعا فالظاهر أنه مبتدأ

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah reads لا تطغوا without أن, with an implied saying and لا prohibitive, as shown by the jussive verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأعبد الله لا تطغوا بغير ( أن ) على إرادة القول

words: فَيَوْمَئِذٍۢ لَّا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذَنۢبِهِۦٓ إِنسٌۭ وَلَا جَآنٌّۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the day the sky splits, no one is asked because people are recognized by their signs; verses that affirm questioning concern another station, according to Ikrima and Qatadah.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يعرفون بسيماهم وهذا في موقف وما دل على السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation places questioning at the reckoning and says questioning is absent when people emerge from their graves.
rows.anchor: وموقف السؤالأعلى ما قيل : عند الحساب وترك السؤال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes affirmations of questioning as rebuke and reproach from negations of questioning as genuine inquiry about the sin.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : حيث ذكر السؤال فهو سؤال توبيخ وتقدير وحيث نفي فهو استخبار محض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reconciliation says the denied question concerns the sin itself while the affirmed question concerns its cause; the author objects that verses affirm questioning about the sin itself.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المنفي هو السؤال عن اذلنب نفسه والمثبت هو السؤال عن الباعث عليه

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi attributes to al-Rida the view that an unrepentant sinner who believed the truth is punished in the intermediate realm and reaches Judgment Day with no sin to be questioned about.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبرسي عنالرضا رضي الله تعالى عنه أن من اعتقد الحق ثم أذنب ولم يتب عذب في البرزخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author emphatically rejects attributing that explanation to al-Rida and says the verse should not be forced into it.
rows.anchor: ولعمري إن الرضا لم يقل ذلك وحمل الآية عليه مما لا يلتفت إليه بعين الرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ذنبه refers to إنس, which is prior in grammatical rank as the passive subject; the singular pronoun follows its grammatical form.
rows.anchor: وضمير ذنبهللإنس وهو متقدم رتبة لأنه نائب عن الفاعل وإفراده باعتبار اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explains the singular pronoun by taking the intended referent to be one individual from humankind.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لما أن المراد فرد من الإنس

rows.speaker: الحسن، عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Amr ibn Ubayd read ولا جأن with hamza to avoid the meeting of two vowelless letters, though the sequence is otherwise permitted by the rule.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد ولا جأن بالهمز فرارامن التقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that criminals are recognized by their signs is a fresh sentence explaining why they are not questioned.
rows.anchor: استئناف يجري مجرى التعليل لانتفاء السؤال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading replaces the expected pronoun with the explicit word criminals to specify that the people concerned are the sinners among humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: قيل : من وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير للإشارة إلى أن المراد بعض من الإنس وبعض من الجن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says their signs are black faces and blue eyes.
rows.anchor: سيماهمعلى ما روي عن الحسن سواد الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes their signs to be the gloom and grief visible on them; other proposed signs include blindness, dumbness, and deafness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما يعلوهم من الكآبة والحزن وجوز أن تكون أموراأخر الكعمى والبكم والصمم

rows.speaker: حماد بن سليمان
rows.claim: Hammad ibn Sulayman reads بسيمائهم.
rows.anchor: وقرأحماد بن سليمان بسيمائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: النواصي is the plural of ناصية, the front of the head; الأقدام means the familiar feet.
rows.anchor: جمع ناصية وهي مقدم الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bā is instrumental, as in taking an animal by its bridle, and the prepositional phrase is the passive subject.
rows.anchor: والباء للآلة مثلها في أخذت بخطام الدابة والجار والمجرور نائب الفاعل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the bā as marking the object and the verb as carrying the sense of a verb that governs it, such as being dragged by the forelock.
rows.anchor: وقالأأبو حيان : إن الباء للتعدية والفعل مضمن معنى ما يعدي بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al may replace the possessive pronoun under the Kufan analysis, while Basrans posit an omitted pronoun; the author says that dispute matters only when a resumptive pronoun is needed here.
rows.anchor: أل فيهما عوض عن الضمير على مذهب الموفيين والضمير محذوف على مذهب البصريين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says an angel joins a sinner’s forelock and feet in a chain behind his back, breaks his back, and throws him into the Fire.
rows.anchor: على ما روي عن الضحاك أن يجمع الملك بين ناصية أحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation has some angels dragging sinners by their forelocks and others dragging them by their feet.
rows.anchor: وقيل : تأخذالملائكة عليهم السلام بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view has angels alternately dragging people by forelocks or feet, treating the conjunction as distributive or; the author says this departs from the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: تسحبهم الملائكة عليهم السلام تارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agent is left unstated because it is self-evident; another explanation says the omission signals God’s greatness.
rows.anchor: وإبهام الفاعل لأنه كالمتعين وقيل : للرمز إلى عظمته

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet swore Hell’s angels were created a thousand years before Hell and grow stronger daily before seizing their victims by forelocks and feet; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن مردويه والضياء المقدسي في صفة النار عن أنس قال : سمعت رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وقعت means happened, and الواقعة is a conventional name or transferred name for the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أيإذا حدثت القيامة على أن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explicitly identifies الواقعة as one of the names of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وصرح ابن عباس بأنها من أسمائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name signals that the Resurrection’s occurrence is certain, as though it had already happened independently of the conditional clause; this is not a vacuous subject-verb repetition.
rows.anchor: وسميت بذلك للإيذان بتحقق وقوعها لا محالة كأنها واقعة في نفسها مع قطع النظر عن الوقوع الواقع في حيز الشرط

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies الواقعة as the cry, meaning the blast in the trumpet.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : ( الواقعة ) الصيحة وهي النفخة في الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says it is the rock of Jerusalem that will fall on Judgment Day; the author calls this baseless.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( الواقعة ) صخرة بيت المقدستقع يوم القيامة وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan treats إذا as a conditional time adverb governed by the following verb وقعت, like other conditional nouns, and says it is not annexed to the clause.
rows.anchor: والعامل فيها عند أبي حيان الفعل بعدها فهي عنده في موضع نصب بوقعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians treat إذا as annexed to the following clause; one view says it loses its adverbial force and is an object of an omitted ذكر.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على إضافتها فقيل : هي هنا قد سلبت الظرفية ووقعت مفعولا به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Another analysis preserves its adverbial force and makes ليس its governor, which the author says al-Zamakhshari’s wording seems to favor.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لم تسلب ذلك وهي منصوبة بليس وصنيع الزمخشري يشعر باختياره

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf prefers an omitted answer as the governor, understood as when the Event occurs, such-and-such will happen; the omission magnifies the event.
rows.anchor: وقيل : بمحذوفوهو الجواب أي ( إذا وقعتالواقعة )

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that no grammarian makes ليس govern the adverb, since it resembles ما and lacks event or temporal meaning; he also says a conditional answer with ليس requires fā.
rows.anchor: وأبو حيان تعقب النصب بليس لا يذهب إليه نحوي لأن ليس في النفي ك ( ما ) وهي لا تعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rebuttal notes that grammarians allow an adverb to attach to ما by interpreting it as انتفى, and apply the same reasoning to ليس.
rows.anchor: صرحوا بجواز تعلق الظرف بها لتأويلها بانتفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that fā is obligatory with the answer to إن because of its operation, whereas its use with إذا is contrary to the default.
rows.anchor: بأن لزوم الفاء مع الأفع الالجامدة إنما هو في جواب إن الشرطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the grammatical debate, the author prefers an omitted answer as the governor; leaving it unspecified creates awe and magnifies the Event.
rows.anchor: الأولى كون العامل محذوفاوهو الجواب كما سمعت وفي إبهامه تهويل وتفخيم لأمر الواقعة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes the clause either as a parenthesis confirming the Event’s certainty or as a circumstantial clause describing it.
rows.anchor: إما اعتراض يؤكد تحقيق الوقوع أو حال من الواقعة كما قال ابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كاذبة is an active participle modifying an omitted noun, preferably نفس rather than مقالة, because people are more commonly described as liars than statements are.
rows.anchor: و ( كاذبة ) اسم فاعل وقع صفة لموصوف محذوف أي نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الواقعة literally means a forceful fall, became a common term for a momentous event, and can also be used specifically for war; here it refers to the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: و ( الواقعة ) السقطة القوية وشاعت في وقوعالأمر العظيم وقد تخص بالحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām marks time: when the Event occurs, no soul remains to deny God’s report; current deniers will then acknowledge it as true.
rows.anchor: واللام للتوقيت مثلها في قولك : كتبته لخمس خلوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading means that no one lies about anything on that day; its soundness depends on holding that no one lies then and explaining the deniers’ oath elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقيل : على معنى ليس في وقت وقوعها نفس كاذبة في شيء من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another reading, no one denies the Event or asks the Hour why it came, whereas people deluded by worldly attractions implicitly deny it now.
rows.anchor: و ( كاذبة ) صفة لذلك المحذوف أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing the Hour as if someone could ask it why it came is a representational metaphor, either imagined or taken literally.
rows.anchor: وفيه استعارة تمثيلية لأن الساعة لا تصلح مخاطبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كاذبة may derive from كذبت نفسه or كذبته, when one’s self deceives, indulges distant hopes, and emboldens a person to attempt a great undertaking.
rows.anchor: وجوز كون ( كاذبة ) منقولهم كذبت نفسه وكذبته

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the lām in that interpretation also marks time: no self will encourage its owner to think it can endure the Event’s severity.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف إن اللام على هذا الوجه للتوقيت كما في الوجه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كاذبة may be a verbal noun meaning discouragement or holding back: the Event has no retreat, like a truthful assault by a powerful fighter.
rows.anchor: وجوز أيضا كون ( كاذبة ) مصدرا بمعنى التكذيب وهو التثبيط

rows.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: A similar explanation is transmitted from al-Hasan and Qatadah.
rows.anchor: وروي نحوه عن الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr’s line uses كذب for a lion holding back from its peers, supporting the sense of refraining or retreating.
rows.anchor: لزهير : ليث بعثر يصطاد الرجال إذا ماالليث ( كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds it clearer to take كاذبة as the Event’s falsehood or denial: its occurrence is true and beyond doubt, like a true assault.
rows.anchor: ويجوز جعل الكاذبة بمعنى الكذب للوقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He likewise finds clearer the sense that the Event is not false in its occurrence but is truth without ambiguity, despite this sense also being narrated from al-Hasan and Qatadah.
rows.anchor: أو على معنى ليس هي في وقوعها كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reservation about the preferred verbal-noun interpretation is that the pattern فاعلة is rare for a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: نعم قيل : عليها إن مجيء المصدر على زنة الفاعل نادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forerunners are the third of the three groups; their mention is delayed despite their precedence in merit so their excellent states can follow, and the unqualified title does not assert precedence in every respect.
rows.anchor: هو الصنف الثالث من الأزواج الثلاثة ولعل تأخير ذكرهم مع كونهم أسبق الأصناف وأقدمهم في الفضل ليردف ذكرهم ببيان محاسن أحوالهم

rows.speaker: عكرمة، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ikrima and Muqatil say they are those who first believed and obeyed when truth appeared, without hesitation or delay.
rows.anchor: فقيل : هم الذين سبقوا إلى الإيمان والطاعة عند ظهور الحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns Hizqil, the believer from Pharaoh’s people, Habib al-Najjar from Ya Sin, and Ali; each preceded his community and Ali was their best.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as those who first acquired certain knowledge and levels of piety beyond faith.
rows.anchor: حيازة الكمالات من العلوم اليقينية ومراتب التقوى الواقعة بعد الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the forerunners as the prophets, who lead the adherents of their religions.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم الأنبياء عليهم السلام لأنهم مقدموا أهل الأديان

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says they are those who prayed toward both qiblas, linking the phrase to the earliest emigrants and Helpers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين : هم الذين صلوا إلى القبلتين كما قال تعالى : ( والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies them as the first to migrate.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هم السابقون إلى الهجرة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says they are those who were first to perform the five prayers.
rows.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه هم السابقون إلى الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report raised from Ibn Abbas says the forerunner is the first to set out for the mosque and the last to leave; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم والديلمي عن ابن عباس مرفوعا أول من يهجر إلى المسجد وآخر من يخرج منه

rows.speaker: عبادة بن أبي سودة
rows.claim: Ubada ibn Abi Sawda says it reached them that the forerunners are those who arrive early at mosques and set out in God’s cause.
rows.anchor: عن عبادة بن أبي سودة مولى عبادة بن الصامت

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says they are those who are first to jihad.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك هم السابقون إلى الجهاد

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says they are first to repent and perform good works.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن جبير هم السابقون إلى التوبة وأعمال البر

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka‘b identifies them as the people of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب : هم أهل القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in al-Bahr describes them as those who accept the truth when given, give when asked, and judge others as they judge themselves.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر في الحديث سئل عن السابقين فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A three-person typology calls the lifelong doer of good a forerunner, the sinner who later repents a right-hand companion, and the lifelong evildoer a left-hand companion.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الناس ثلاثة فرجل ابتكر الخير في حداثة سنه ثم دام عليه

rows.speaker: ابن كسيان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan defines them generally as those who hasten to everything God calls them to.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كسيان أنهم المسارعون إلى كل ما دعا الله تعالى إليه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some prefer Ibn Kaysan’s general definition and treat most of the other identifications as examples of it.
rows.anchor: ورجحه بعضهم بالعموم وجعل ما ذكر في أكثر الأقوال من باب التمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common parsing makes the repeated phrase a topic and its predicate, meaning the forerunners are renowned and their greatness is well known.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فالشائع أن الجملة مبتدأ وخبر والمعنى ( والسابقون ) هم الذين اشتهرت أحوالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the noun as its own predicate magnifies the forerunners and signals their widely known merit, as illustrated by the quoted boast about Abu al-Najm’s poetry.
rows.anchor: أبو النجم وشعري شعري وفيه من تفخيم شأنهم والإيذان بشيوع فضلهم

rows.speaker: صاحب المرشد
rows.claim: An alternative gives the two occurrences different objects: first to God’s obedience and then to His mercy, or first to good and then to Paradise; the first formulation is attributed to Sahib al-Murshid.
rows.anchor: وقيل متعلق السبق مخالف لمتعلق السبق الثاني أي السابقون إلى طاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the ordinary predicate reading: it is complete without assigning different objects to each occurrence, and is more eloquent and fitting here.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الحمل مفيد بدون ذلك كما سمعت بل هو أبلغ وأنسب بالمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a topic and predicate, serving as an explanatory resumption.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ وخبر والجملة استئناف بياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A competing parse makes the first السابقون the topic, the repeated word its emphatic confirmation, and أولئك المقربون the predicate; the author rejects it as weakening the division, the rhetoric, and the following contrast.
rows.anchor: وقيل ( السابقون ) السابق مبتدأ ( والسابقون ) اللاحق تأكيد له وما بعد خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولئك points to the forerunners; its distant demonstrative form despite the nearby antecedent signals their exalted rank.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بأولئك إلى السابقين وما فيه من معنى البعد مع قرب العهد بالمشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المقربون describes those granted closeness and standing with God.
rows.anchor: و ( المقربون ) من القربة بمعنى الخطوة أي أولئك الموصوفون بذلك النعت الجليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators explain the close ones as those whose ranks have been brought near to the Throne.
rows.anchor: وقال غير واحد : المراد الذين قربت إلى العرش درجاتهم

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad takes each group label as the predicate of an omitted topic: the expected next step after dividing people is to name the categories, then describe them.
rows.anchor: الذي تقتضيه جزالة التنزيل أن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: On al-Irshad’s analysis, the descriptions of the first two groups are parenthetical previews of their eventual states, while the forerunners receive their description immediately and need no preview.
rows.anchor: خلا أنه لما أخر بيان أحوال القسمين الأولين عقب كلا منهما بجملة معترضة بين القسمين

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshad parses السابقون as a topic, with explicit repetition for grandeur; أولئك begins a second topic or is appositional, and المقربون supplies the predicate.
rows.anchor: فقوله تعالى : ( السابقون ) مبتدأ والإظهار في مقام الإضمار للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds al-Irshad’s analysis more natural: after division, the categories themselves are expected as the primary point, rather than a judgment about them or their descriptions.
rows.anchor: والذي يتبادر للنظر الجليل ما في الإرشاد من كون أصحاب الميمنة وكذا كل من الأخيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A criticism says al-Irshad’s parse does not itself give detailed states, but identifies the groups while alluding generally to their astonishing conditions; it also asks why the two questions about the other groups would be omitted from the detail.
rows.anchor: وقيل عليه : إنه ليس في جعل جملتي الاستفهام وقوله سبحانه : ( السابقون ) إخبارا لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further analysis allows the two questions to modify their preceding group labels after an implied saying, and السابقون likewise to modify its antecedent; the following clause then resumes explanatorily.
rows.anchor: بل يجوز أن يكون كل منهما صفة لما قبلها بتقدير القول كأنه قيل : فأحدها أصحاب الميمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that this adjective analysis deletes a relative pronoun and part of its clause, the author denies that أل is relative when it does not indicate a new occurrence.
rows.anchor: وما يقال : إن في هذا الوجه حذف الموصول مع بعض أجزاء الصلة يجاب عنه بمنع كون أل في الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it a noble Qur’an glorifies and confirms the preceding oath.
rows.anchor: وهو تعظيم للقسم مقرر مؤكد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical لو تعلمون falls between the adjective and the noun and intensifies the glorification; its unanswered conditional either denies their knowledge or implies that they would revere it or act accordingly.
rows.anchor: وقوله عز وجل ( لو تعلمون ) معترض بين الصفة والموصوف وهو تأكيد لذلك التعظيم وجواب ( لو ) إما متروك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatness of the oath has been indicated earlier, and is especially clear if مواقع النجوم is understood as Ibn Abbas and others transmitted.
rows.anchor: ووجه كون ذلك القسم عظيما قد أشير إليه فيما مر أو هو ظاهر بناءا على أن المراد ( بمواقع النجوم ) ما روي عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi explains كريم as excellent and pleasing among its kind of books, or as abundantly beneficial; the benefit fits a Qur’an containing foundational knowledge for this life and the next, with generosity used metaphorically.
rows.anchor: ومعنى كون القرآن كريما أنه حسن مرضي في جنسه كمن الكتب أو نفاع جم المنافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes generosity broadly to include praiseworthy qualities such as great benefit, making the description literal.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الكرم أعم من كثرة البذل والإحسان والاتصاف بما يحمد من الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also mean noble in God’s sight; the author says this returns to the prior sense and requires an unnecessary implied preposition.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد كريم على الله تعالى قيل : وهو يرجع لما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an itself, not merely to its status as a recitation; the point is that it was revealed to the Prophet rather than composed by him, as disbelievers claimed.
rows.anchor: قيل : إن مرجع الضمير هو القرآن لا من حيث عنوان كونه قرآنا فبمجرد الأخبار عنه
